lines.en: Hi! **I’d like to rent** a bike for the day.
lines.pt: Oi! Eu gostaria de alugar uma bicicleta por um dia.

lines.en: Sure. A city bike or a mountain bike?
lines.pt: Claro. Bicicleta urbana ou de montanha?

lines.en: A city bike. **How much per day?**
Twenty dollars. The helmet is free.
lines.pt: Vinte dólares. O capacete é grátis.

lines.en: Yes, a hundred dollars on your card. You get it back.
lines.pt: Sim, cem dólares no cartão. Você recebe de volta.

lines.en: It’s covered if it’s stolen. Please lock it. Show me your ID.
lines.pt: Está coberta se for roubada. Por favor, tranque. Me mostre o seu documento.

lines.en: Here you go. Is six o’clock OK to return it?

situation.text: You are visiting a city for the weekend and want to rent a bike. At the rental shop you need to know the price, the deposit and what you must bring.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can rent a bike or a car: ask the price per day, ask what you need, check the insurance and agree on the return time.
canDo: Ask the price: How much per day?
Ask what you need: Do I need…?
Ask about insurance: Is it insured?
success: I say what I want to rent.
I ask about price and rules.
I agree on the return time.
pages.think: Have you ever rented a bike, a scooter or a car? What did the company ask you to show?

group: Cada estudante diz UMA palavra que associa à situação de hoje.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso: é a missão final da aula.
extra: Would you rather rent a bike or a car on vacation?
What do you need to show to rent something?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

errors.w: I go to work by foot.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Renting a bike or a car in the USA comes with a few rules and papers. Guess before you read.

cards.note: To rent a car you usually need a valid driver’s license and a credit card.
Many shops hold money on your card as a deposit and give it back when you return the item.
Helmet rules differ by state and city. Many shops give you a helmet.

qs.q: What do you need to rent a car?
qs.pt: O que você precisa para alugar um carro?

levels.A2: You need a driver’s license and a credit card.
levels.B1: A valid license, a credit card and often a minimum age, such as 21.
levels.B2: Companies usually set age limits and extra fees for young drivers, so it is worth checking the terms.

levels.A1: Money you leave. You get it back.
levels.A2: It is money held on your card until you bring the item back.
levels.B1: The shop keeps an amount on your card as a guarantee and releases it when you return the item.
levels.B2: A deposit covers possible damage or loss and is usually released once the item is returned in good condition.

qs.q: Do people wear helmets on bikes?
qs.pt: As pessoas usam capacete na bicicleta?

levels.A2: Many people do, and it is safer.
levels.B1: It is common and recommended, and some places require it, especially for children.
levels.B2: Laws vary by state and city, but safety experts recommend helmets for everyone.

pages.compare: In Brazil, you also show your CNH to rent a car, and a deposit on the card is common. Helmets for cyclists are more of a recommendation. What is it like where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que o estudante compare com a sua própria experiência no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.

Q2: valor retido no cartão e devolvido.

Mostre o texto só depois da 2ª escuta.

Compare as respostas entre as duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 2: city bike · twenty dollars · a hundred dollars · ID · six.
extra: Who is speaking? How do you know?
Which word did you catch first?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Say what you want to rent.

items.alt: Also: **How much is it a day?**

items.use: Ask what you must have or do.
Ask what comes with the rental.

items.en: What time do I return it?

items.use: The clerk asks to see your ID.

items.en: I’d like to rent a car.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Peça um exemplo próprio para cada expressão ★.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Compare equivalentes formais e informais em duplas.
answers: Prioritárias: I’d like to rent… · How much per day? · Do I need…? · Is it insured?
extra: Which of these would you say to a friend? To a stranger?

errors.w: Do I need of a license?

support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Rental request
patterns.formula: **I’d like to rent** + a / an + noun
ex: I’d like to rent a bike.
I’d like to rent a car for two days.
I’d like to rent a helmet too.

patterns.name: Do I need…?
ex: Do I need to pay now?

patterns.name: Prices per time
patterns.formula: **How much** + per day / per hour / for the week?

Written English

register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules: contracts and websites use the written forms.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais; os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).

Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.

extra: Change one word and say the new sentence.

stretch: Combinar dois padrões na mesma fala.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Final sounds matter: “need” ends with /d/, “deposit” has a clear /t/, and “day” does not end with a consonant. Don’t add an extra vowel.

opts: Do I need a deposit it?

own.prompt: Write your own “Do I need…?” question about something you rent.
own.criteria: Say it twice: first slowly, then naturally. Do you hear the final /d/ in “need”?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: Final consonant sounds.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar → reproduzir ritmo e entonação → usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e normal; peça que o estudante bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria.
answers: Identify 1: Do I need a deposit? · Identify 2: Is it insured?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

Se acertar rápido, peça a versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: I’d like to rent a bike, please. · 2: How much per day? · 3: Do I need a deposit? · 4: Is it insured?
Gap: like · per · Do I need a license? · Is the helmet included? · Here you go.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — rent a bike or a car

brief.teacher: You are the rental clerk (add a change: the bike is not available!).
brief.student: You are the customer: rent something and ask about price, rules and insurance.

orders: A city bike for the day
A small car for the weekend
complications: The bike you wanted is not available.
The deposit is higher than you expected.
You forgot your ID: explain calmly.
You return the bike late: apologize and ask about a fee.
success: I say what I want to rent.
I ask about price and rules.
I agree on the return time.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida do estudante (um lugar que ele realmente frequenta).
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if the bike has a problem? What do you say?

errors.r: I’d like to rent a bike.

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Peça que o estudante compare duas opções (bicicleta × carro) e escolha uma, explicando por quê.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo). Com 6 estudantes, três duplas simultâneas.

Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.

Do I need a license for the car?

pages.title: Group mission — rent your ride
pages.goal: Each group rents something in English: say what you want, ask the price and the rules, and agree on the return time.

missions.mission: Rent a city bike for one day. Ask the price and if a helmet is included.
missions.constraint: Use “I’d like to rent…” and “How much per day?”

missions.mission: Rent a small car for the weekend. Ask what you need and about the insurance.
missions.constraint: Use “Do I need…?” and “Is it insured?”

missions.mission: Your rental is late. Say you are sorry and ask if there is a fee.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m sorry” and ask one question.

success: Say what you want to rent.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “I’d like to rent a bike.” → “City or mountain?” → “City. How much per day?” → “$20.” → “Do I need a deposit?”
extra: What if the other person does not understand you?
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a rental shop: ask if they have a bike for Saturday and what you need.
pages.model: Hello! **I’d like to rent a bike on Saturday.** How much is it per day? Do I need a deposit? Thank you!
checklist: I said what I want to rent.
I asked about price or rules.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos entre colegas e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more question for the clerk.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: I’d like to rent a bike.
ladder.goal: Rent something with short phrases, models and pictures.

ladder.say: How much per day? Do I need a deposit?
Is insurance included, or do I have to pay extra?
Could you walk me through what the deposit covers, in case I return it slightly late?
I’d like to be sure I understand the terms before signing, particularly the clause on damage.
Were the bike to be damaged through no fault of mine, would the deposit still be forfeit?
ladder.goal: Use conditional structures and precise legal wording.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
